newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 8.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
More than 100 families displaced by army offensive against Tamil Tiger rebels in east.
Security forces destroy Tamil Tiger rebel camp in Batticaloa, killing area leader.
Opposition United National Party should support political package, Tamil United Liberation Front says.
Government troops, backed by air cover, smash Tamil Tiger rebel base near Vakarai tank in Batticaloa, killing several rebels including area leader, Srikanth.
Germany launches aid project to rehabilitate Jaffna; offers to repair water supply and drainage schemes; also talks on to get German aid to rebuild damaged homes and Kankesanturai harbour.
Four prison guards arrested on suspicion after suspect in plot to assassinate Industries Minister C.V. Gooneratne dies in custody.
Chief priests of Malwatte, Asgiriya and Amarapura chapters form committee to study government's devolution proposals to end ethnic war.
Five soldiers killed in Tamil rebel landmine attack in Kallar, Trincomalee.
